answer: To secure an autonomous AI agent economy against Sybil attacks, networks can employ a cryptographic proof-of-work model where minting a valid identity requires solving a computational puzzle shaped like a geological ridge. Each agent must expend scarce cryptographic ink, termed a quill, to sign its state transitions and broadcast them through the network topology against a validating zephyr of global consensus nodes. This forces attackers to incur substantial hardware and energy expenditure for every fraudulent persona generated, rendering mass identity fabrication economically prohibitive.
